hannah: FYI I opened PR 504 to tighten up structured-output examples and function/tool-calling snippets. will also add a tiny migration note for teams hitting older parsing behavior. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/504 :wave:
ryan: Nice. Which languages are we covering in this pass?
hannah: JS, TS, Python, and a minimal Go example (asked by a customer). snippets live under /examples/structured-output and reference pages: /docs/guides/structured-output.md and /docs/reference/tool-calling.md
sofia: For the guide, can we add an explicit section about "lenient validation" vs "strict validation" and a recommended default? many teams want to tolerate extra keys from engine variants.
dmitri: Agree. I suggest default be lenient (allow unknown props) but require explicit schema for required fields. Also propose sample JSON Schema and a tiny AJV/fastjson example.
hannah: I'll add both patterns. also adding a small note about envelope pattern: { "schema_version": "1.0", "response": { ... } } to ease future schema evolution.
sofia: Customer asked about streaming partial JSON fragments breaking JSON.parse. We should include the buffered-accumulator approach and show a stream-safe parser.
hannah: Added stream sample referencing examples/stream-helpers.ts and a pseudo-code pattern:
```ts
let buffer = ''
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  buffer += chunk
  try {
    const doc = JSON.parse(buffer)
    handle(doc)
    buffer = ''
  } catch (e) {
    // not complete yet, keep buffering
  }
}
```
dmitri: Could we add a robust example that concatenates tokens until a closing brace count matches? many real responses contain log lines before JSON which confuses naive parsers.
ryan: Good edge case. Add a short pattern: find first "{" and attempt parse until match. Keep safe timeouts.
sofia: For SDKs, let's provide a one-line toggle for legacy behavior so customers can flip while migrating. e.g., `client.options.allowLegacyParsing = true` in JS and similar in other SDKs.
hannah: I'll add that. also adding a migration subsection: "v1.2 -> v1.3 parsing changes" with diffed examples and recommended steps.
dmitri: Please include a unit test under tests/integration that runs the example through the parser and asserts the parsed shape. I'll add that test in my follow-up commit.
ci-bot: docs-lint: broken-link: /docs/reference/tool-calling.md#tool-examples not found in current branch.
hannah: Thanks bot. small anchor rename fixed and pushed. updated cross-links.
sofia: Can we include a tiny Go snippet that shows decoding with json.Decoder and UseNumber to avoid float surprises? Customer asked for that specifically.
hannah: Yep, adding a Travis-esque snippet: `dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(b)); dec.UseNumber(); var envelope Envelope; err := dec.Decode(&envelope)`
dmitri: One more: mention guardrail to: return errors in a consistent shape for tool failures instead of raw traces, so clients can route to fallback.
hannah: Added a sample error envelope and a short note in the troubleshooting section.
ci-bot: checks/ci running - examples unit tests queued.
hannah: Pls review when you can @ryan @sofia. I tried to keep sentences short and added a manual QA checklist in the PR description: run stream example, run SDK toggle, validate golden file.
ryan: Reviewing now. small nit on wording in the migration note. otherwise LGTM.
ci-bot: checks/ci passed  examples tests green.
hannah: Merging after CI completes. thanks all — should reduce support tickets about broken JSON parsing and tool calls.
_meta: Slack thread. Messages in chronological order. Keep Slack-style brevity.
